scope: Supplementary source-local check of the unresolved English number/coordination in the shared Qatadah-Ata-Ikrimah statement on al-Salat in Qurtubi 108:2. This extends the existing Q05 checkpoint; it does not replace it or approve a new translation.

prior_stage.prior_observation: stored English renders صلاة العيد as 'the prayer of the two Festivals' and also carries ويوم النحر as 'the Day of Sacrifice'

english.source_phrase: Qatadah, Ata', and Ikrimah said: “Pray to your Lord” refers to the prayer of the two Festivals and the Day of Sacrifice, and “sacrifice your offering.”

source_anchors.locator: Sura 108:2, rendered page 602, first issue, online line 21
source_anchors.witness: وقال قتادة وعطاء وعكرمة : فصل لربك صلاة العيد ويوم النحر . وانحر نسكك .
source_anchors.finding: The source groups the three named authorities under a single وقال clause; the excerpt names no individual route or isnad. The phrase presents صلاة العيد followed by ويوم النحر.

source_comparison.textual_number_observation: In the Arabic witness the expression is singular-form صلاة العيد; the text does not state العيدين (the two Eids). The stored English explicitly pluralizes it as 'two Festivals'.
source_comparison.coordination_observation: Arabic includes the conjunction و before يوم النحر; the stored English preserves an 'and' but combines the plural 'two Festivals' with the separate Day of Sacrifice phrase.
source_comparison.translator_boundary: This is a demonstrable form/number discrepancy and translation hold. It is not, by itself, sufficient to decide whether singular al-'id is generic, whether the phrase is appositional ('Eid prayer on the Day of Sacrifice'), or whether a different rendering is warranted. Do not settle that question or replace the English without independent scholarly review.
source_comparison.reviewer_control_gloss: For comparison only, a close control rendering is 'the Eid prayer and the Day of Sacrifice'; this is not an approved translation or a proposed live replacement.
source_comparison.attribution_boundary: Keep Qatadah, Ata, and Ikrimah as the three authorities expressly grouped by Qurtubi. Do not invent separate transmission routes or attribute the cluster to a different work based on derivative websites repeating the same wording.
source_comparison.independent_witness_limit: This check uses the primary online Qurtubi witness and unchanged live Arabic/English rows; search results repeating the same Qurtubi passage are not counted as independent evidence.
